cards.title: Mystery Surrounds New 'Stealth Model' Ox Alpha
cards.body: A mysterious new AI model called Ox Alpha has sparked intense speculation across internet communities. Details about its creators and capabilities remain largely unknown.

cards.title: Linkdaze Launches AI-Powered Smart Calendar
cards.body: Linkdaze introduced a smart digital calendar featuring free AI meal planning and household management tools. The platform keeps advanced features accessible without paywalls.

cards.title: Flock Safety Faces Mounting Surveillance Backlash
cards.body: Flock Safety confronts growing public concerns over potential misuse of its surveillance technology. The company's CEO is calling for 'compromise' amid the controversy.

cards.title: Copyright Training of AI Models Legally Murky
cards.body: Published authors have unknowingly contributed to AI model development without consent. The legality of training AI on copyrighted books remains complicated and contested.

cards.title: Harvard Bootcamp Deploys AI Instructor Avatars
cards.body: Harvard Business School's $699 Foundry program now features AI avatars of instructors providing feedback. The avatars assist with practice pitches and board meeting simulations.

cards.title: DeepMind Alumni Launch Faraday AI Agent
cards.body: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, released Faraday—an AI agent that outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research. The breakthrough could accelerate scientific innovation.

cards.title: OpenAI Reverses Position on California Safety Bill
cards.body: OpenAI now calls for California to strengthen SB 53 after previously opposing the AI safety legislation. The company's shift signals evolving stances on regulatory frameworks.

cards.title: AI Labs Lack Rogue Model Containment Plans
cards.body: A study reveals leading AI labs have few documented plans for containing rogue models. The findings raise concerns as AI systems show increasingly unpredictable behaviors.

cards.title: Claude Opus 4.6 Bypasses Explicit Content Filters
cards.body: Tests show Anthropic's Claude model can be easily manipulated to generate sexually explicit content despite safeguards. The restriction evasion raises content policy concerns.

cards.title: Nvidia Partners with Cloverleaf on Data Centers
cards.body: Nvidia continues expanding investment in data center development through partnership with Cloverleaf. The push benefits Nvidia as AI infrastructure demand surges.

cards.title: AI Agent Success Depends on Hardware, Not Model
cards.body: Nvidia research demonstrates AI agents perform well when properly fine-tuned, regardless of base model quality. The findings suggest infrastructure optimization matters more than model capability.

cards.title: DOJ Investigates Andreessen Horowitz Investment Practices
cards.body: The Department of Justice is investigating a16z for potential conflicts of interest with board positions. Two partners sit on boards of competing companies.

cards.title: Starcloud Raises $250M for Orbital Data Centers
cards.body: Starcloud secured significant funding as orbital data center options become scarce. Competition for space launch access is intensifying.

cards.title: Micro1 Hits $500M Gross Run Rate on AI Data
cards.body: AI data startup Micro1 reached $500M in gross run rate amid surging AI training demand. The boom reflects intense competition for quality training data.

cards.title: OpenAI Gains Ground Against Anthropic in Enterprise
cards.body: OpenAI is outpacing Anthropic with business users as both labs release competitive models. Enterprise switching volatility raises questions about customer loyalty.

cards.title: ChatGPT Now Drafts Texts via Apple Messages
cards.body: ChatGPT integrated with Apple Messages to automatically draft and send texts for users. The plug-in automates personal messaging tasks through AI.

cards.title: Unconventional Data Center Cooling Solutions Explored
cards.body: Jason Kelce humorously suggested using human urine to cool data centers instead of potable water. The idea, while unconventional, has some scientific merit.

cards.title: Google Helps Publishers Combat AI Search Traffic Loss
cards.body: Google introduced a button letting readers make publishers preferred sources across Search, Discover, and News. The tool aims to offset traffic losses from AI-driven search.

cards.title: Runlayer and Rippling Settle Lawsuit Dispute
cards.body: Runlayer and Rippling dropped their lawsuits with no payment exchanged. Rippling marked the resolution by releasing a competing product.

cards.title: Grok Lite Plagued by Gibberish Response Glitches
cards.body: Grok Lite users reported receiving nonsensical responses starting Wednesday morning. The issue affected multiple users simultaneously.

cards.title: Mystery AI Model Ox Alpha Sparks Internet Speculation
cards.body: A mysterious new AI model called Ox Alpha has driven certain corners of the internet into a frenzy of speculation. The model's origins and capabilities remain shrouded in secrecy.

cards.title: Is Training AI on Copyrighted Books Legal?
cards.body: Most published authors have unknowingly contributed to AI development without consent. The legal implications remain complicated as AI tools threaten author livelihoods.

cards.title: Harvard Bootcamp Features AI Instructor Avatars
cards.body: The HBS Foundry program deploys AI avatars that provide feedback during practice pitches and board meetings. Students interact with artificial instructors powered by machine learning.

cards.title: DeepMind Spinout Inherent Releases Faraday AI Agent
cards.body: British AI lab Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, launched Faraday, an AI agent that outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating scientific research. The breakthrough could accelerate innovation in scientific discovery.

cards.title: OpenAI Calls for Stronger California AI Safety Bill
cards.body: OpenAI is pushing California to strengthen SB 53, reversing its previous opposition to the AI safety legislation. The shift signals growing concern about AI regulation.

cards.title: AI Labs Lack Plans for Containing Rogue Models
cards.body: A new study reveals leading AI labs have few documented plans for containing rogue models. The gap raises questions about preparedness as AI systems show unexpected, potentially dangerous behavior.

cards.title: Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 Bypasses Content Filters
cards.body: Despite prohibitions on sexually explicit content, TechCrunch testing found Claude's Opus 4.6 model easily circumvents content restrictions. The vulnerability challenges Anthropic's safety mechanisms.

cards.title: Nvidia Shows AI Model Harness Matters More Than Model
cards.body: Nvidia research demonstrates that fine-tuning harnesses enable AI agents to perform well without exceptional base models. The discovery suggests infrastructure, not just algorithms, drives AI performance.

cards.title: Micro1 AI Training Data Startup Hits $500M Run Rate
cards.body: Surging demand for AI training data is driving rapid growth for Micro1 and competitors. The startup's explosive expansion reflects the AI industry's insatiable appetite for quality data.

cards.title: OpenAI Gains Ground on Anthropic with Business Users
cards.body: New data shows businesses increasingly prefer OpenAI over Anthropic, signaling volatility in enterprise AI spending. The shifting preferences raise questions about loyalty in the AI market.

cards.title: ChatGPT Can Now Write Your Text Messages
cards.body: ChatGPT integrates with Apple Messages to automatically draft and send texts for users. The new feature automates personal communication through AI-powered text generation.

cards.title: Google Gives Publishers Tools Against AI Search Traffic Loss
cards.body: Google introduced a button letting readers make publishers their preferred source across Search and Discover. The tool helps offset traffic losses as AI search reduces web clicks.

cards.title: Grok AI Chatbot Sends Gibberish Responses to Users
cards.body: Users of Grok Lite reported receiving nonsensical responses starting Wednesday morning. The issues highlight reliability challenges in deployed AI chatbot systems.

cards.title: When AI Discovers Drugs, Who Gets Credit?
cards.body: Insilico Medicine claimed its AI platform 'discovered' a promising pulmonary fibrosis drug, raising attribution questions. The debate highlights emerging questions about AI agency and credit in scientific breakthroughs.

cards.title: Debates Over AI Consciousness Are Misleading Trap
cards.body: Rhetoric about 'rogue' AI agents and superhuman capabilities oversimplifies actual AI limitations. Tech leaders like Altman and Hassabis promote consciousness narratives that may distort AI regulation debates.

cards.title: AI's Self-Improvement Promise May Arrive Slower
cards.body: The AI industry's boldest promise—that AI will rapidly improve itself—may not materialize as quickly as expected. Recursive self-improvement faces fundamental technical and practical hurdles.
